Sebagaimana diketahui, we're just past the midway point of the nfl season, which means it's time to start thinking seriously about who has and has not met the expectations we set for them at the start of the year. Everyone came into the season with a different set of hopes, and everyone has had plenty of time to meet, exceed or fall short of them now that we have played nine weeks of football.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for some teams, whether they have done what was expected of them is fairly obvious: the chargers have not, for example. For other teams, it's not so obvious: The entire NFC South would fit that description. But what about the rest of the teams in the league? How have they performed, and how would we grade them relative to what was expected of them entering the season?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that's why we're here. We're assigning letter grades to each team's performance through the midway point of the season. We broke down where each team stands, and why, below.

Berdasarkan laporan, dallas came into this season with high hopes but has instead disappointed. The Cowboys' defense remains a disaster, and the offense hasn't lived up to expectations. They've also blown a couple of games with poor situational football awareness. The only thing saving them from a worse grade is that the rest of the NFC East is bad enough that they're in second place and potentially in position to make a run at the playoffs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, notwithstanding their thursday night loss to washington, the giants could hardly have hoped for the start of the john harbaugh era to go any better results-wise. They're in first place in the division despite having lost their starting quarterback in the second game of the season. Rookie Arvell Reese looks like a total monster. They have mostly won close games, so they might not be as good as their record indicates, but that doesn't matter when it comes to how they've performed relative to expectations.

Berdasarkan laporan, the eagles would have an f if not for howie roseman's smart pivot to selling off pieces at and around the trade deadline, which restocked the cupboard full of draft picks for the future. Philly is always smart about knowing when to pull the plug on a lost season, which is exactly what this year has been.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the commanders weren't necessarily expected to be all that competitive in the nfc east this year, but the degree to which they've fallen behind the giants and cowboys is disappointing. The game management issues under Dan Quinn have also persisted, which contributes to this grade.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the bears, like the rest of the nfc north, have to be happy with how their season has gone to date. The offense looks explosive, and the defense looks better after the addition of Jeffery Simmons. The only thing holding them back from getting a straight 'A' here is the surprising lack of run game efficiency, though Kyle Monangai's absence has contributed to that.

Berdasarkan laporan, the lions have one of the most explosive offenses in the league, with jahmyr gibbs, amon-ra st. Brown, Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta combining with Jared Goff to light up scoreboards. The defense has even been playing better lately, albeit in light matchups. There have been some issues here and there (like the loss to the Panthers), but overall, things have gone quite well relative to expectations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the packers have to be thrilled with how their season has gone. The one thing holding them back from an 'A' is how they started the season, with a bad loss to Minnesota and the blowout against Atlanta. Jordan Love is playing near an MVP level. Despite the absence of Micah Parsons, the defense has been excellent. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden look like superstars. Otherwise, things have gone about as well as could be expected.

Berdasarkan laporan, the vikings' defense gets an a+++++, but the offense has been bad enough to knock the team down nearly a full letter grade despite minnesota's 6-2 record. Here's hoping that Kirk Cousins can at least prop things up a bit for the rest of the season.

Diungkapkan bahwa i can't justify giving any nfc south team anything other than a 'c' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.

Berdasarkan laporan, same as above: i can't justify giving any nfc south team anything other than a 'c' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i'll say it one more time: i can't justify giving any nfc south team anything other than a 'c' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sorry, this is the last time: i can't justify giving any nfc south team anything other than a 'c' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.

Berdasarkan laporan, the cardinals have actually been better than anybody expected. That said, getting a second-round pick back for Marvin Harrison Jr. Things will also likely get worse the rest of the way, given their injury issues. They do have five double-digit losses, though, so it's hard to give them a grade in the 'B' range. They have three wins, and they've played a couple of other close games mixed in there. looks like a good deal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the super team expectations were probably always a bit too high, but the rams haven't come close for a variety of reasons. Being over. Whether it's injuries, Matthew Stafford's regression or even more injuries, you have to dock the Rams for not even being a surefire playoff team at the midpoint of the season. 500 despite the injuries is mildly impressive, but not enough to give them a grade in the 'B' range.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the 49ers are a team that has overcome nearly as many injuries as the rams have faced. It seems like as long as they have Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle, they are just going to keep humming. And Raheem Morris has the defense playing well despite its own injury issues. They've been great on both sides of the ball.

Berdasarkan laporan, we initially had the seahawks at a 'b-' grade, but then we remembered the odd loss to the commanders in week 3 and had to knock them down. Seattle has navigated some offseason losses (Klint Kubiak, Kenneth Walker III and more) and injury issues (the entire backfield), and three of its four losses came in one-score games, but we expected the Seahawks to be closer to the top of the division than they are right now.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the bills have overcome a questionable defense to emerge midway through the season with a 7-1 record. Josh Allen is firmly in the MVP mix once again. The offense has kept humming despite DJ Moore missing time. James Cook is averaging even more rushing yards per game than he did a year ago. The Joe Brady era is off to a very good start.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the dolphins have played right around expectations so far this year. They have smartly played at a snail's pace on offense to try and shorten games and stay competitive, which has resulted in them losing by less than expected in some contests, and they even beat the Jets. Still, it's hard to justify better than a 'C' grade when you're 1-7 at the halfway point.

Diungkapkan bahwa the patriots' start to the season was terrible. But they've lost two games against good teams over the last three weeks, and they got smacked by the Packers in the most recent one. They then got on a little bit of a run to bounce back, and it looked like they might recapture some of what they had last year. The injury issues on offense matter, but sitting at 5-4 before their trip to Munich is a slight disappointment.

Berdasarkan laporan, the jets look like they have a nice corps of young players on both offense and defense, but they're also 2-7. It's hard to find the appropriate grade for that type of team, especially when it's coming off its worst loss of the season, where it was totally non-competitive. It feels like a 'C+' is just right, relative to what we expected from them coming into this year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, considering they haven't had lamar jackson for much of the season (he basically played 3. 5 games), it's at least somewhat impressive that the Ravens are still in the mix in the AFC at 4-5. But they've lost four games in a row and have looked inept offensively of late (albeit in brutal situations), and Jesse Minter's defense hasn't been able to make up for it.

Diungkapkan bahwa the bengals' offense started the season somewhat slowly, as per usual, but has kicked into high gear of late, as per usual. Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are basically unstoppable, and the defense is improved relative to recent years. There have been some ups and downs with that unit (27 points against the Bucs despite four turnovers, 30 against the Steelers, 24 against the Dolphins despite three turnovers, 36 against the Titans despite two turnovers), so that's keeping them from earning a straight 'A' here.

Berdasarkan laporan, the browns are 5-4, which would make you think they should get an 'a' relative to expectations. But when you look at the context of those games, and the fact that they each required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes, you see that the record isn't as impressive as it looks on the surface. Still, the wins count, and five is probably more than many people expected them to get coming into the year.

Diungkapkan bahwa the inexcusable loss to the browns back in week 4 keeps the steelers out of the 'a' range, which they might otherwise be in, given their offense and defense. The run game has been impressive, and the defense has maintained a high level of play. Coming out of their bye at 6-2 is an ideal midseason result.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the texans are 3-5, and two of their wins have come against the titans and chargers. Their defense has regressed year over year. That all overshadows the great season they're getting out of C. J. Stroud, who has been even better this year than he was during his spectacular rookie season.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the colts have been a disaster on both sides of the ball and had to enter fire-sale mode. This grade would be lower if not for the fact that they did get some assets for a few players who were obviously on their way out the door.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the jaguars are 6-2 with two one-score losses, and they look elite on both offense and defense. They might have an inside track on the No. 1 seed in the AFC, given their rest-of-season strength of schedule. We docked them to an 'A-' thanks only to the frankly bonkers price they paid in the Jordan Davis trade, even if he is going to help their defense the rest of the way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the titans looked more competent in their final three games going into their week 9 bye, even if they did lose two of them. The offense looked so bad early in the year, though, that we can't even justify giving them a straight 'C' here. We're grading the entire season to date, not just what's happened most recently. Getting a second-round pick and more for Amani Hooker was nice, though.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i don't know how the broncos keep getting away with it in one-score games (6-0 this season), but they do. They're probably not as good as their 6-2 record suggests, and they got embarrassed in the season opener against Kansas City, but there's no denying their track record of winning in clutch situations at this point. So, we're giving them a bit of credit for it here.

Diungkapkan bahwa the chiefs have taken care of business for the most part this season, losing only to the seahawks and broncos on the road in back-to-back weeks. The blip in Weeks 7 and 8 counts, though, and it revealed an inability to find a way to win if Kenneth Walker doesn't go off. They have otherwise been able to run the ball at will on everyone, and their defense has been excellent. That matters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, things worked out quite nicely for the raiders. They started out 3-0, Kirk Cousins played well enough to give Fernando Mendoza time to sit and learn for half a season, and then they got a third-round pick for Cousins at the deadline. If they hadn't lost five of their last six games, this grade would be even higher.

#812. Rethinking How Teams Plan, Make Decisions And Work Together

📅 13 Nov 2026

Rethinking How Teams Plan, Make Decisions And Work Together

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2026/11/13/rethinking-how-teams-plan-make-decisions-and-work-together/

Deniz Gezgin is CEO of Eightpoint, a global technology company building & scaling consumer digital products across mobile & desktop.

Diungkapkan bahwa ​when i became ceo of eightpoint in july 2024, i joined a company with experienced teams and strong technical capabilities across desktop and mobile software. I saw an opportunity to connect that expertise more closely and build a company where teams could make decisions with a clearer understanding of the broader business.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we’ve spent much of the past two years working through that change. Bringing different functions together around shared priorities has required us to revisit how information moves through the organization and how decisions are made.

Berdasarkan laporan, that experience has shaped my perspective on ai. As new tools make development, analysis and testing more efficient, the way a company operates becomes increasingly important.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the first things i noticed was how much time could be lost between capable teams working toward different priorities. Engineering, product, analytics and marketing each had valuable expertise. When information stayed within individual departments, teams sometimes approached similar problems independently or made decisions without the full context.

Diungkapkan bahwa we’ve worked to bring shared capabilities—including data, platform and design—closer to our product teams. This gives people access to expertise across the company and helps reduce duplicated effort.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i believe leaders introducing ai should pay close attention to these existing workflows. Understanding where decisions slow down can reveal opportunities to improve how the organization works as a whole.

Diungkapkan bahwa annual and quarterly planning remain useful for establishing direction and allocating resources. At the same time, product teams often receive meaningful feedback long before the next formal planning review.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve become more interested in organizing execution around shorter learning cycles while keeping longer-term business priorities consistent. A team can work toward an annual objective while using two-week sprints to evaluate specific assumptions, make improvements and determine where to focus next. Our product development approach emphasizes defining a problem, testing an idea and using the results to guide additional investment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are limits to how frequently a company can change direction. Teams need enough stability to complete meaningful work, and some decisions require more time to evaluate.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as a ceo, i’ve learned that the way leaders make decisions has a significant influence on how quickly the rest of the company can move. During periods of change, it’s natural to want greater visibility into what’s happening across the business. I’ve had to think carefully about where my involvement is useful and where it can slow people down.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’ve been working toward clearer ownership across our teams. That comes with expectations around accountability. I want leaders to understand the outcomes they’re responsible for, have access to the information they need and feel confident making decisions within their areas. People need to explain their reasoning, make results visible and raise issues early enough for the organization to respond.

When an experiment produces an unexpected result, I want to understand how the team approached the decision and what it recommends doing next.

Berdasarkan laporan, ai’s creating opportunities for teams to produce more work in less time. As that happens, I think leaders need to become more thoughtful about how they evaluate progress. Traditional measures such as features delivered, campaigns launched and projects completed remain useful, but they provide only part of the picture.

I’m interested in how quickly teams can validate assumptions, identify problems and apply what they’ve learned.

Diungkapkan bahwa in consumer software, the results of an experiment can be difficult to interpret. A change might improve engagement among one group of users while having little effect elsewhere. Teams need time to understand those differences and determine whether the improvement supports the broader product.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this requires a culture where people can discuss disappointing results openly. I’ve found that the way leadership responds in those moments has a lasting influence on how teams approach future decisions.

Berdasarkan laporan, culture becomes visible in the everyday decisions people make. One of our priorities has been creating stronger connections between the teams responsible for developing products, understanding users and growing the business.

Berdasarkan laporan, for example, bringing spigot and eightpoint technologies together under the eightpoint brand gave us a shared identity. The more involved work has been making that identity meaningful through clearer priorities, stronger ownership and better collaboration.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve learned that encouraging people to work together only goes so far. They also need shared information, aligned objectives and a clear understanding of who’s responsible for moving decisions forward. The relationships between people and the trust required to make decisions together still need attention from leadership.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m encouraged by the practical ways ai is already supporting our work. Our desktop team is using AI-assisted tools for browser upgrades and automated testing, with human approval remaining part of the development and release process.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as these capabilities develop, i expect companies will have more opportunities to experiment and respond to changing user needs. Leaders will need to think carefully about how they organize teams, allocate resources and create room for learning.

I’m proud of the progress we’ve made, particularly the broader ownership our leaders have taken and the way teams are becoming more connected.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for me, the opportunity ahead is to build a company that can keep improving its products, its decisions and the way people work together. The progress we make will depend on how thoughtfully we put those capabilities to work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, jeremy pearlman: okay. Great. Yes. Understood. And maybe, yes, so you just touched on it at the very end, just to segue to my next question. Just as a reminder, the 510(k) pathway is the lowest hurdle for a medical device to go through FDA approval -- FDA clearance, and it just requires a substantial equivalence to an existing predicate device. Look, we can get a little bit in the weeds on that for those who are students of 510(k) versus De Novo. The next stage is the De Novo, which is -- has a higher -- it is between the 510(k) and the PMA and has somewhat higher requirements with regard to the clinical study design, the size and so forth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when portio was actively being pursued before we paused the project several years ago, our engagements with fda had led to a determination at that point that this was likely -- that this needed to go down the de novo pathway. What's happened since that engagement with the FDA are 2 things. One, we had our first-in-human study, a successful human study in Colombia, South America that demonstrated the safety of the device in humans. That's how we were proceeding before we paused the project. That wasn't available at the time of the original engagement with the FDA.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, also, on further analysis with our team as well as with external regulatory consultants, some of whom were actually -- were aware of the previous application, it's become clear to us that the major consideration with regard to moving this down the de novo pathway had to do with the predicate device was used for urgent and emergency situations and portio is not really intended for that. The purpose of PortIO is to be a long-term vascular access device comparable to existing ports and existing long-term catheters.

Diungkapkan bahwa we have a possibility, and i think a reasonable possibility that we -- this time around, we can proceed on a 510(k) basis by simply saying that we're not -- that the intended use does not include emergency and urgent insertion, which is consistent with sort of the commercial strategy anyway. Both of them will be fine. We're confident based on the previous data and based on the previous conversations that we have a clear path to completing a study and getting this cleared.

But obviously, our strong preference would be to be able to do so through the 510(k) pathway, which would be shorter and less capital -- less capital requirements and potentially might not even need additional human data, but that's still to be determined.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jeremy pearlman: okay. And then just lastly, moving to Octeris. Great. Maybe help investors understand what is it -- what type of -- what problem is it trying to solve? Is it creating a better mousetrap? Is there any other standard of care current competitors that are tackling the same issue? And maybe that would be really helpful.

Diungkapkan bahwa lishan aklog: yes. Excellent. EsoGuard identifies these patients with precancer, they go for an endoscopy. That's the paradigm under which these patients are being managed. You can consider this basically the Octeris to fit in, in the post- EsoGuard step. Obviously, most folks in PAVmed have some understanding of the detection of esophageal precancer and its management to prevent esophageal cancer, obviously, because EsoGuard -- the EsoGuard test is designed to identify patients with esophageal precancer and send them to a confirmatory endoscopy to determine the subsequent management of that patient, whether it be surveillance, or an ablation treatment to treat the late-stage precancer. Then at the time of endoscopy, what are the various things that can be done to enhance that.

Diungkapkan bahwa the direct answer to your question is that octeris does compete with some existing technologies. Most of them are molecular tests that seek to risk stratify patients or to determine at the time of confirmatory endoscopy, whether the patient needs more aggressive surveillance, whether there's a likelihood that they have the later-stage precancer and maybe should be directed more towards an urgent -- more immediate treatment with ablation. There's a variety of technologies that are out there and molecular tests that are out there that seek to be supplements to the confirmatory endoscopy.

Berdasarkan laporan, octeris has the opportunity to make essentially most of those obsolete because what it does, instead of using a molecular test, it uses imaging, a combination of optical coherence tomography as well as an additional more proprietary optical method to assess the areas of abnormality at the time of endoscopy. So we can look at those cells and it's able to measure the size of the nucleus, which correlates very closely with the likelihood that they have late-stage precancer, which would need to be treated more directly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that's a bit in the weeds, but the bottom line is that when octeris is finalized and commercialized, it will provide the opportunity to take a patient who has suspected precancer, suspected barrett's esophagus, hopefully, from having gotten an esoguard test and during the endoscopy to determine whether that patient has a late-stage precancer and whether those areas should be biopsied more aggressively. Then if it does come back as dysplasia the later-stage precancer, whether that patient should go straight to the definitive treatment. Over the long-term, later versions of this device, the goal would be to have it be a onetime procedure.

Diungkapkan bahwa you go in for your confirmatory endoscopy and the endoscopist assesses the area and using the supplemental imaging from octeris, they can decide to ablate and destroy those abnormal cells on the spot, eliminating the need for multiple other interventional procedures. That's the paradigm that we're operating within. If it is successful, it really will shake up the way these patients are managed after they are identified as having precancer.

Operator: Your next question comes from Ed Woo with Ascendiant Capital.

Berdasarkan laporan, edward woo: congratulations on all the progress. Are you guys mainly focused on your 4 devices now, Lucid, Veris, Octeris, PortIO? Or are you guys also actively looking for new portfolio products?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lishan aklog: yes. We do continue to evaluate those. With that, as always, we encourage you to continue to keep abreast of our progress. Please follow us through our news releases, these update calls at our website and through social media. Of course, feel free to reach out with any specific questions.

With that, I hope you all have a great day, and thank you so much for your participation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, fed meetings, global news. you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Berdasarkan laporan, this morning, the bureau of labor statistics released the producer price index for october, which tracks the change in prices that u. S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the results were mixed. 0. 3% vs. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0. 4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6. 5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Berdasarkan laporan, investors are convinced that the federal reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in december to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0. 5 to 0. 75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

Berdasarkan laporan, with rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7. 76% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

Berdasarkan laporan, if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

Berdasarkan laporan, nerdwallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#820. The Cognitive Enterprise In 2027: Four Priorities For AI Maturity

📅 13 Nov 2026

The Cognitive Enterprise In 2027: Four Priorities For AI Maturity

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2026/11/13/the-cognitive-enterprise-in-2027-four-priorities-for-ai-maturity/

Casey Kindiger is a technology entrepreneur and CEO of Droma (formerly Grokstream).

Sebagaimana diketahui, ​when a customer reports a service disruption, different parts of the business often see different problems. Operations sees an infrastructure alert, finance sees a billing exception, and account management sees a renewal at risk. Each team may have AI tools to interpret its information, yet connecting those perspectives still requires people to exchange messages, reconcile records and find someone who remembers a similar incident. AI is accelerating individual tasks, but it is also exposing a fundamental weakness in how enterprises operate: Intelligence remains fragmented, even as the technology becomes more capable.

Berdasarkan laporan, as organizations prepare for 2027, closing that gap should become a leadership priority. A recent McKinsey article, citing its latest state of AI survey, reports that 80% of respondents say AI has improved their individual productivity, while only 37% report a positive impact on earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT). That gap illustrates the challenge ahead: Translating local improvements into better business outcomes requires changes to how information, decisions and responsibility move across the enterprise.

Having spent much of my career building operations automation and AI systems, I see four priorities for measurable AI maturity in 2027:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the cognitive enterprise offers a useful framework for this transition. Generative AI now makes institutional knowledge more accessible, while agentic AI can pursue objectives through multiple steps and systems. The concept predates generative AI; IBM described it in its 2019 annual report as an organization informed by data and AI and equipped to adapt. What is different now is the possibility of a more explicit cognitive architecture: systems that connect perception, institutional memory, judgment, governed action and learning across the enterprise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these capabilities bring the vision closer, but their usefulness depends on the information and authority available to them. An agent cannot reliably resolve a customer issue when account records disagree, procedures are outdated or responsibility for approving a remedy is unclear.

Berdasarkan laporan, after years of building businesses around it operations and ai-driven automation, i’ve learned that identifying a problem is rarely the hardest part. The greater challenge is connecting what the organization knows to the decisions it needs to make—and ensuring those decisions lead to meaningful outcomes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the organization also needs to connect technical evidence with business context and carry that understanding across teams as they decide what to do. Otherwise, each department can become more efficient while the overall process remains slow, inconsistent and dependent on a few experienced employees.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a modern cognitive enterprise connects six capabilities: sensing changing conditions, retrieving institutional knowledge, evaluating possible responses, governing authority, acting within defined boundaries and learning from verified outcomes. Institutional knowledge includes why a previous response succeeded, which assumptions proved wrong and when an exception was justified. This requires more than access to documents. Together, they support a continuous process in which new information informs decisions and the results improve subsequent work. Making that context available helps teams evaluate unfamiliar situations without reconstructing every decision from scratch.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the service-disruption example, a connected workflow could associate technical symptoms with affected customers, retrieve previous remedies, assess service commitments and recommend a coordinated response. A reversible technical action might proceed automatically, while a consequential service change would require approval. The resulting value includes less repeated investigation, fewer contradictory recommendations and shorter delays between identifying a problem and resolving its business consequences. Customer-facing teams could receive the same verified account of what happened and what comes next. Recording the outcome also gives the organization a stronger basis for responding when conditions change again.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as ai systems gain the ability to act across systems, governance becomes part of the architecture that makes useful autonomy possible, not a control layer added afterward. Access to information should not automatically confer authority to change a system or make a customer commitment. Each workflow needs an accountable owner, clear limits on automated action and a record of the evidence supporting consequential decisions. Human reviewers need sufficient context to evaluate recommendations, along with practical ways to pause, redirect or reverse execution.

Berdasarkan laporan, my view, informed by work in operational ai, is that broader responsibility should follow demonstrated performance on the decisions a system will actually handle. A system that identifies missing evidence and requests assistance can be more useful than one that produces a confident response to every situation. Learning requires comparable discipline: Teams should verify an action’s effects before treating it as a precedent. Otherwise, an apparent success can reinforce a flawed assumption or conceal costs transferred to another department.

Berdasarkan laporan, leaders can begin with one workflow that crosses departmental boundaries and has a measurable consequence, such as service restoration, customer onboarding or order exception handling. Map where work stalls, where employees repeatedly search for information and where handoffs lose context. That foundation should include authoritative sources, consistent definitions and named owners responsible for keeping information current. Establish baseline measures for completion time, rework, errors and customer impact, then identify the knowledge needed to improve those results. Employees who manage exceptions should help shape the design because their experience often reveals gaps in formal procedures.

Berdasarkan laporan, before enabling automated action, define what ai may recommend, what it may execute and when it must escalate. The more important measure is whether each resolved case improves the starting point for the next one. Teams can then extend the same information sources, decision rules and safeguards to related workflows, allowing enterprise intelligence to develop incrementally. Evaluate results across the complete workflow, including downstream workload and oversight costs, before extending the approach. AI maturity should increase not only execution speed but learning velocity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 2027, ai maturity won’t be measured by the number of agents deployed or tasks automated. It will be measured by whether the enterprise becomes more capable because of the work it has already done—turning experience into better judgment, safer action and faster learning.

Sebagaimana diketahui, forbes technology council is an invitation-only community for world-class cios, ctos and technology executives. Do I qualify?.

Berdasarkan laporan, as a bettor, my focus is instantly looking at the week 10 games and futures market for value that ripples as an effect of these transactions. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the soft tank is on in philadelphia. This team has lost seven straight games and they are without QB Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season. After turning to Tanner McKee at QB after Hurts' injury news broke, they quickly stopped that experiment, signed Joe Milton off the Cowboys practice squad and he is now starting. I truly think the Eagles know this season is lost, they don't want to win and prefer to prioritize upcoming draft capital. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the eagles have a very forward-thinking front office. Davis was given a huge signing bonus when Philadelphia inked his deal, and thus his annual salary was lower and his trade value was higher. One reason they were able to get a first-round pick for Davis was because of his team-friendly contract. Those little edges the Eagles gain are indirect ways to show they will prioritize next season over squeezing out an extra win or two.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i expect milton to remain the starter and players that are injured — like devonta smith with a hamstring issue — to be kept out as long as possible. An injury that a player might have played through on a contending team will now be a reason to sit out.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i am betting the eagles regular-season win total under 4. 5, hoping they don't win three of their final eight games.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fernando mendoza, the no. The other side of this is looking at Mendoza's competition for this award.

Diungkapkan bahwa there have been no standout players who are leading the pack for oroy. Broncos rookie RB Jonah Coleman and Titans WR Carnell Tate round out the top three with the shortest odds. In terms of the terms of our debt, we reduced its duration from 11. 7, it is a very efficient debt that the company has. In the next slide, I will conclude my presentation with this slide on taxes. 8 to 6. We achieved record production levels this year, and we also paid record amounts in taxes.

Diungkapkan bahwa it was brl 251 billion in taxes in nine months, an increase of brl 50 billion compared with the same period last year. We are creating more value for our shareholders and for the entire Brazilian society. We will now start the Q&A session, and I will give the floor to Eduardo.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, fernando. Our first question comes from Gabriel Barra with Citigroup. Gabriel, please feel free to open your mic.

Berdasarkan laporan, gabriel barra: can you hear us? hi. I will stick to one question as requested, and I believe mine is a very simple question. We have seen a significantly more challenging geopolitical environment in the last few years, which has had several impacts, and as a consequence, the oil price, fuel prices in general have been impacted. The President mentioned this. Hi, President Magda, Fernando, and other directors. Thank you so much for taking my questions. Now, if you were looking at the current timeframe and thinking of politics, understanding that the company will remain adherent to its policy throughout the fiscal year, I'd like you to tell me how would you assess Petrobras' price policy, especially thinking of diesel and gasoline.

Berdasarkan laporan, i wonder if you believe any sort of adjustment to prices would be required throughout the rest of the year, and especially in early 2026, considering that recent times have been quite troubling. I just wonder if there could be any carryover to next year, a potential waiver, or any increase in fuel prices if you decide not to adhere to today's current accounting policy.

Diungkapkan bahwa eduardo de nardi ros: thank you so much for your question. I will turn it over to Director Angélica Laureano to address it. Good afternoon, Gabriel. It's a pleasure to speak to you.

Berdasarkan laporan, angélica laureano: well, first of all, i'd like to remind all of you how our policy has been conceived. I'd also like to remind you that over the last 10 days, we saw a $25 variation in oil prices. It was conceived so as to enable Petrobras to work and operate in any market conditions while reconciling aspects such as competitiveness, value generation, and production, not passing through to the rest of the market any volatility that there might be in the market. If that type of volatility were to be transferred to the market, that would generate great uncertainty.

Berdasarkan laporan, petrobras, according to its policy, and i'd like to restate that its commercial strategy remains in place, and it is steady, and we'll continue to work in that sense. What we're discussing is how to operate in quite a troubling geopolitical environment such as the one we're faced with. But at this time, we do not think of any structural change to our policy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, angélica. Once again, thank you, Gabriel, for your question. Let's move on to the next question that's coming from Regis Cardoso with XP. Regis, can you hear us?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, regis cardoso: good afternoon, eduardo and all petrobras directors. Thank you so much for taking my question. I ask that because to us, the average for the fiscal year seems to be consistent with your policy, especially if you consider the diesel export price parity. I'll also stick to this one-question policy. Still on the issue of price, I know we'll be discussing investments as well, which is another topic of interest. But that's not the case for gasoline. It seems far from the VM bands.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i don't know if i'm being too technical about the specifics of the policy, but if you could maybe detail it a little bit more. Again, this is Angélica, Regis. As a reminder, our policy is or consists of the CAC, which is the client alternative cost, and VM, which is our best alternative cost, Petrobras' alternative cost. I don't know if this is a year where there's a force majeure in place, or if we should think of it in any other way. Thank you. It is within those ranges that we've been working with our policy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, angélica laureano: evidently, we are not making specific assessments, but rather within a larger context. I think it is important to highlight that ours is a very consistent strategy, and it is not determined by today's snapshot, but rather by the context at large. As I said in my previous answer, we are currently in internal discussions to understand whether there is a need for any change, any non-structural, but rather situational change to that policy, considering our current scenario.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, angélica, and thank you, regis, for your question. Let's move on to our next question that comes from Bruno Amorim with Goldman Sachs. Bruno, do you hear us?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bruno amorim: good afternoon. I can hear you well. I have a question about your investment plan for the next few years. Hi, good afternoon. Thank you for taking my question. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i just wanted to understand whether that investment that we saw this year entails a lower capex next year. Thank you.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, bruno. Again, I will move that to Director Renata.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, renata baruzzi: hi, bruno. What happened was our risk analysis was based on past events, and in fact, we have been able to deploy as planned. When we assess things for our plan, we run a risk analysis to check how confident we are in our CapEx deployment. Good afternoon. Our CapEx deployment this year led us to this. We have been able to mitigate execution risks and deliver a larger volume of oil, as you saw, whether you look at it via interconnection or by well. Part, or the most part of that CapEx surplus took place within the E&P. Within that, most of that came from the platforms, most of which are performing at an outstanding level.

Sebagaimana diketahui, p-84, just to give you an idea, has had most of its structure completed. To mitigate the risk of simultaneous operations, we are moving a lot of those activities forward for this year. We are preparing for the lines, for perforation, because the Búzios field is really clogged up because of the number of platforms, and all of which are several boats offering supply and removing material that is not necessary. Next year, we plan to keep up the same pace. P-83 will start navigating next year, and we are gearing up for the delivery of this platform. We are already doing that with regards to several projects, many of which had already been secured.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as was said earlier, we are always looking to move forward on our timetables for our projects. This year, we had planned to conclude 44 wells, and to this day, we have already concluded 19. I will give you a few examples. It is about having a more effective CapEx that will lead to earlier production. That entails higher production. When we talk about increasing the capacity of our platforms, we need a higher number of wells to connect to those platforms, and that is where our output is coming from. That's what we see for next year and for our investments with regards to what's already in our plans.

Berdasarkan laporan, what we've been doing with our supply department is to stay resilient or to keep our suppliers resilient, many of which are in brazil and have increased their production capacity to serve us. With regards to that, we've already increased our vendor base to deal with that. That's a bottleneck that we're facing. As you all know, data centers are a huge competitor of the oil industry because of the gas turbines. With a number of steps, with all departments in tandem, we've been able to keep our CapEx and our projects within budget.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fernando melgarejo: i just wanted to add something here, bruno. Our strategic plan for 2031 will be delivered on November 23rd, and that should give you an updated overview of all the investments we plan to have in our next cycle. I'd also like to add that this CapEx increase was planned in a well-managed way, part and parcel of our cash generation, at which pace we increased our investments and understood that would bring more benefits, which is why we're predicting an increase of about 103,000 additional barrels per day in 2026.

Diungkapkan bahwa magda chambriard: thank you. I just wanted to add two things to what Renata and Fernando mentioned, which I think should be stressed. We have one asset that delivers significantly, which is our pre-salt prospecting. First of all, as you all have seen, we've been working in expanding the capacity of our installed facilities, and I mean specifically our platforms, which is where most of our cost comes from. Platforms ultimately limit the capacity for oil delivery from these deep oil wells. What we're doing is to deliver results, and you're seeing the results that come from that increase in production.

Berdasarkan laporan, i had already mentioned a decline of about 10%, seeing as we work with a non-renewable source of energy, so there's a decline to the tune of 10%. So in 11 platforms, but as I've mentioned earlier, there are also 182,000 barrels a day. That's how we approach the expansion of our installed capacity. We've improved the management of our deposits with higher water injection and more systematic monitoring, and that decline has now turned into a 3% decline. What do I do with that? We need to produce or to bring outcome to make up for that. We need more oil from our deposits. There's something that we do in the near-term, which is to interconnect our wells.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you monitor petrobras' outlays in subsea installment, as renata mentioned, we plan to interconnect 44 wells throughout the entire year, and by the end of q3, we had connected 49, meaning we have another quarter to interconnect a number of other wells. Obviously, we're talking about investments that had not been accounted for in our business plan, but it's still a short-term investment, which we call non-recurring investment. Whenever we talk about increasing capacity, we're saying we've added, with no extra CapEx, 282,000 barrels to our capacity per day. On top of that, there's another issue. That's about 250,000 platforms.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you think that each one of these could cost from $3 billion-$5 billion, we are talking about a non-investment to the tune of $7 billion. There is also an absolutely priceless value, which is the time for a new platform. We are saying that when we increase capacity as quickly as we have had with the existing platforms, we no longer need to hire new units, so we also save CapEx there. We are saying even more than that. When we sign a contract for a new platform, whether that is our own platform or a chartered one, we could count at least four years until it is delivered.

Diungkapkan bahwa think about what four years of anticipating 280,000 barrels a day. Those of you who are analysts can run the numbers, but anticipating that amount of production has an absolutely unquestionable value anywhere in the world for any oil company in the world. Even more than that gives you a comparison basis against all P-80 platforms, and I mean by that P-82, P-83, P-84, and P-85, each of which predict an increase in production to the same tune of what we see with Almirante Tamandaré. That, as you may remember, was the first of 225,000 barrels a day capacity. Capacity for 225,000 barrels a day that has been exceeded substantially.

Berdasarkan laporan, that platform is now licensed to operate with 270,000 barrels a day, so 45,000 barrels a day more than expected. When we add these 282,000 with the production of these five new platforms that are coming into production, we are talking about an increase in capacity of about 500,000 barrels a day in total, meaning a CapEx savings to the tune of between $10 billion and $12 billion. This June, I kindly invite you to check out my LinkedIn post, as well as the Petrobras website, where we reported that it produced 262,000 barrels a day. Again, as I said, at least four years earlier than expected. So it is absolutely invaluable that which we have achieved.

Sebagaimana diketahui, definitely, when you purchase a platform, you will have to account for its expenses throughout its lifetime. This CapEx effect is absolutely specific, which, when you think about the company's management, makes all the difference. Over and above that, when we came to this company's management, we had construction work that was delayed beyond their expected timetable. By early 2024, Petrobras' actual investment was to the tune of 70% and not 100%.

Berdasarkan laporan, now, we are performing 100% of what had been planned, and even more than that, when we look at p-84 and p-85, we expect a potential early delivery of about eight months in advance, and for p-85, of over one year, another record, another feat that had never before been seen in this company. All this which you are seeing is what has led to the balance that we are delivering today, and we are deeply proud of presenting it today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, madam president, fernando, renata. He is with Morgan Stanley. Let us now move on to Bruno Montanari's question. Thank you, Bruno, for your question. Bruno, can you hear us?.

We are working towards that. We have until the 22nd to close ranks on that issue. It is a major player in the resin global marketplace.

Berdasarkan laporan, yes, the board is within the strategic plan effort to increase petrobras' synergies with braskem when it comes to refinery. Diungkapkan bahwa eduardo de nardi ros: thank you so much for your question, monique. We will hand it over to Fernando, who will take your question.

Berdasarkan laporan, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, milene. I will be turning over to our director, Sylvia, to take your question.

Tasso, feel free to go ahead.

Berdasarkan laporan, i wanted to understand where the company would be more comfortable with those prices or maybe make a decision about them, considering that we're approaching the end of the year, and every day that passes, any need of a price increase would have a more limited on the average for the year, which would maybe reinforce the decision for an alternative path. Thank you.

Berdasarkan laporan, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you for your question, tasso. Again, I will turn it over to Director Angélica.

Diungkapkan bahwa angélica laureano: hi, tasso. That is our policy. Our policy presupposes that we should be constantly seeking the VM level moving toward our CAC. Remembering once again that VM is our marginal value, which accounts for production, imports, and our best market condition, and CAC, which is the alternative client cost. We do not have a break-even Brent price for our policy. That is essentially our policy. What we seek is to stay within that range between the CAC and the VM. So there's no such thing as a break-even Brent price for us.

What we seek is to constantly reach the CAC, which is the client alternative cost, which, as I said a few times here, the landscape is very complex this year, which is why we are looking into perhaps a situational alternative to better address these market shifts that we are facing this year.

Diungkapkan bahwa eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, angélica, and thank you for your question, tasso. Our next question comes from Leonardo Marcondes with Bank of America. Leo, go ahead.

Diungkapkan bahwa fernando melgarejo: thank you. Let me start with the foreign exchange impact, which is by over $1 billion to normalize our overall CapEx. Renata has the details, and she'll be adding to my answer.

Diungkapkan bahwa renata baruzzi: as i'd mentioned earlier, 40% of our capex increase derived from the better performance and construction of new platforms. With P-79 in operation, P-80 and P-82, which are already poised to go into operation, and also with P-85, we've doubled the physical progress versus last year. So these are projects that are very much ahead of schedule, and as our President has mentioned earlier, we are working intensely on making progress on these platforms. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we've also moved forward the completion of our interconnections in búzios 8. We're also moving forward the third and fourth producers in Búzios with P-79. So we're also seeking to move forward the P-79 production for next year. As I mentioned earlier, there were also increased investments in wells. We're working diligently to have that production come earlier as well. Every Búzios 8 well are already interconnected, which makes us a lot more confident in our production. The wells we had planned for completion for the year at large, we completed in September.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you so much. Do you hear us, Jorge? I do, yes. Our next question from Jorge Gabrich from Scotiabank. Good afternoon. Thank you for taking my question.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you for your question, jorge. I'll turn it over to our Director, Sylvia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sylvia anjos: hi, jorge. With the Equatorial Margin, Submarine Amapá, and also deep waters results, just to compare with other wells, it took us nine wells to discover the entire basin of Campos, a few wells for the Santos Basin, and fortunately, in well number one, we found not only one, but three different deposits with a huge potential. In terms of action, we are now concluding the Morpho well with these results. Yeah, that's right. Outside of that, we have six blocks where we have a 100% stake, and our obligation as a minimum prospecting program, we have to drill at least seven new wells. Other five are already expected within those, but we do not have the environmental license for them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, our prospecting efforts will now be focused on the morpho well, where we've already mapped out three different wells. Before that, the drill that's operating in Rio Grande will be drilling Mãe de Ouro. Following that, we'll have the NS-43 drill that will be coming up to that area. In that area, we might see a new front of positive discoveries opening up. We already have the license to operate on them, and that will be our next activity. We're very confident about that.

Berdasarkan laporan, in summary, we had 15 wells predicted in our plan, and i believe there's much that we can do over the next five years with these 15 wells, and we are fully on schedule in that sense. That new front should open up in the state of Amapá, potentially, and also in Rio Grande do Norte.

Diungkapkan bahwa eduardo de nardi ros: thank you, sylvia, and thank you, jorge, for your question. Our next question is coming from Vicente Falanga with Bradesco BBI. Vicente, please move ahead.

If you'll allow me, I'd like to take the opportunity to use this forum to go back to your price policy again, because I think the market, Ecopetrol, a state-run oil company from Colombia, they have the numbers which are published to the market every quarter, and this is widely accepted, and it generates an accommodation for risks, so to speak, that's very interesting. That was my question.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eduardo de nardi ros: thank you so much for your question, vicente. I will turn it over to Director Angélica Laureano again, who will be answering your question.

Angélica Laureano: Vicente was his name, right?.

Berdasarkan laporan, angélica laureano: hi, vicente. We should remember that, as I said time and time again, our policy attempts not to pass on any volatility to the market. #833. AI Agents Are Only As Good As The Tools They Can Reach

📅 13 Nov 2026

AI Agents Are Only As Good As The Tools They Can Reach

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2026/11/13/ai-agents-are-only-as-good-as-the-tools-they-can-reach/

Jennifer Artabane is SVP of Product Management at Auros, with 20+ years of experience in enterprise software, health tech and e-commerce.

Diungkapkan bahwa every serious software company supports model context protocol (mcp) now. In under two years, MCP has gone from experimental to an assumed offering. According to a December 2025 Stacklok survey, almost half of the responding technical leaders from the software industry stated they were using MCP in production.

Berdasarkan laporan, mcp support on its own no longer distinguishes anyone. Best-in-class MCP is now an expectation, and the question is now what your agents can reach through MCP? For product teams, the answer that matters is real customers and the ability to learn from them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while agents have made building fast, they haven’t accelerated learning from customers in the same way. The teams that pull ahead are the ones that fold customer insight into every stage of the AI product development life cycle instead of running it as a separate step tacked on at the end.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for 20 years, product development has been getting quicker. The AI-native product development life cycle (AI-PDLC) is the latest turn of that screw. Agents draft specs, generate prototypes, write code and run QA. The stages are the same, but the speeds at which they’re completed aren’t, with AI and humans now working together on those tasks. Work that used to require a sprint can now fill an afternoon.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the same is happening to research, validation and feedback loops, going from cycles measured in weeks to cycles that can happen in hours or days. The goal is to learn at the same pace you build so you can keep moving fast without losing sight of what you’re building and why you’re building it in the first place. Human feedback needs to be rigorous but doesn’t need to slow down development. ​.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if a build only takes hours, a feedback study with customers at the end of the life cycle that takes too long will offset any speed gains your ai-pdlc earned you. However, that study is nonnegotiable. It has to be done. This juxtaposition wasn’t present in previous development shifts because AI output looks finished but is rarely complete and must be validated.

Diungkapkan bahwa we worked with zigzag, a puppy-coaching app, to develop and refine its ai chat feature, ziggy. In the first six months, Ziggy had received a 96% positive customer rating, been used over 80,000 times and helped cut human trainer support requests by 27% thanks to constant, high-quality user feedback. The team ran numerous tests throughout development using real-time customer feedback to decide which features were ready for release. ​.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, customer feedback is most valuable when it comes back to a product team in a time frame that enables it to iterate rather than rebuild the product. This is even more true if agents and AI are involved in what you’re developing or making; that end-user feedback will make or break it, and it needs to come in quickly. ​.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, gathering that feedback is now shifting from a stage in the life cycle to a capability available at any point in it. An agent can put a question to real people mid-task the same way it queries a database or pulls a document. MCP has made this possible. Research-based MCP servers let teams recruit participants, create studies and launch tests from Claude, ChatGPT and all other LLM-based tools, such as Figma Make, without leaving that tool. ​.

Diungkapkan bahwa when results are ready, they can be accessed from the same place, making it easy to incorporate into next steps. This approach changes how the research is completed and actioned but also who it’s for; increasingly, the primary users of customer research are people and agents in equal measure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the obvious shortcut, tempting as it may be, is to simulate the feedback with synthetic users only. Synthetic user insights can be useful, but companies should exercise caution. Models are built to produce the most likely answer, so asking one model to validate another’s output may confirm what’s typical and miss what’s surprising.

The moments of surprise are where the product value sits, so don’t forgo the user or customer.

Diungkapkan bahwa start by mapping where in your product development you want to reach a real customer. Most teams find agents own the build steps entirely but have no route to customer input until a human commissions a study. This is where the change needs to happen, giving agents access to that human insight early on.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, remember to treat agent access to people as a governance decision rather than a feature switch. For that, you’ll need rules for spend (so recruitment costs don’t run unchecked) and rules for approval (so a person signs off before an agent launches anything).

Good governance is essential, and I’d suggest product leadership keep three questions in mind here:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, 1. At what stage of our life cycle can an agent ask a real customer a question?.

Berdasarkan laporan, 3. Are we measuring how fast we build or how fast we learn?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mcp support became table stakes within two years. Agent-driven build speed is heading the same way. Once every team can build in hours, the advantage belongs to the organization that incorporates real customer insight into its AI-PDLC and gets it back quickly. #839. The Four Pillars Of Data Readiness For Agentic Commerce

📅 13 Nov 2026

The Four Pillars Of Data Readiness For Agentic Commerce

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2026/11/13/the-four-pillars-of-data-readiness-for-agentic-commerce/

Chuck Yu is CEO of VGS, a trusted infrastructure powering payment tokenization and agentic commerce for the world’s leading enterprises.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ​it seems like there are protocols created, updated and evolving almost every week in agentic commerce. Part of my job is understanding them. While this shift unlocks new conversion potential, it also introduces a troubling new reality for merchants: a growing data blind spot at the exact moment they can least afford one.

Diungkapkan bahwa as agentic commerce scales, merchants risk becoming passive endpoints in a transaction chain they can no longer fully see. I don’t see the problem as the technology itself, but it’s that the current infrastructure, when dealing with an agent, obfuscates data that merchants have historically relied on to detect fraud, build loyalty and understand their customers.

Merchants who understand the pillars and advocate for access to them will be positioned to thrive in agentic commerce.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when a legitimate shopping agent crawls a merchant’s website, it looks virtually identical to a malicious bot. Amazon currently blocks traffic from certain AI platforms for exactly this reason. Without a standardized way to distinguish between the two, merchants face an impossible choice: Block automated traffic and lose valid conversions, or accept all traffic and risk fraud. Mastercard recently contributed its verified intents framework to the FIDO Alliance. Until standardized agent identification is universally adopted, merchants remain vulnerable on both ends. I think this is a wonderful starting point, and we will likely see much of this approach with substantial staying power.

Diungkapkan bahwa in traditional e-commerce, merchants use frameworks like 3ds to verify that a real, authenticated person is behind a transaction and tag that user for future fraud detection and dispute resolution. Agentic commerce breaks this model. When an agent handles verification on the consumer’s behalf, the merchant is removed from that process entirely. They include two-factor authentication, often including the consumer’s financial institution. Shopify and Stripe have been particularly effective at embedding themselves at the point of the consumer-agent handshake. Most current approaches involve the agent undergoing enhanced consumer verification. ​.

Sebagaimana diketahui, here’s a scenario every merchant should internalize: a consumer instructs their agent to buy an end table for no more than $500. The agent moves on. A merchant sells one for $501. The merchant never makes the sale and has no idea why.

Diungkapkan bahwa scale that across thousands of shoppers with identical agent configurations, and you have a merchant losing significant volume by a single dollar, with zero visibility into the signal. Consumer mandates, such as price ceilings, preferred brands and shipping requirements, govern every decision an agent makes. Today, merchants receive none of this information. If even aggregate mandate data were passed to merchants, the implications for dynamic pricing and real-time promotions would be incredibly informative.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the end of an agentic transaction, a merchant typically receives one of two things: an agentic network token or a virtual card. This lets the receiving PSP settle the transaction. But the token is single-use, carries no traceable lineage and cannot be stored for loyalty programs, subscriptions or card-on-file relationships. Money moves. The merchant receives confirmation that a sale occurred, but not the contextual intelligence that would make that sale meaningful beyond its immediate revenue impact.

If merchants wait for a perfect data infrastructure before engaging in agentic commerce, they will find themselves behind competitors already adapting.

I see the four pillars—agent identification, identity verification, consumer mandates and payment credentials—as a representation of the minimum viable dataset for merchants to participate in commerce not as passive endpoints, but as informed commercial actors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these data gaps are not inherent to agentic commerce. They are design choices that can be redesigned. Merchants who engage now in standards bodies, protocol conversations and infrastructure decisions will help shape a more transparent ecosystem. Those who wait will inherit whatever architecture others build for them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the agent economy will create enormous opportunities. The question is whether merchants will be ready to meet it. ​.

#846. Your Attacker's AI Knows You Better Than Yours Does

📅 13 Nov 2026

Your Attacker's AI Knows You Better Than Yours Does

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2026/11/13/your-attackers-ai-knows-you-better-than-yours-does/

Founder and CEO at CYFIRMA, overseeing the business strategy, product roadmap, growth & expansion plan, and investor relationship.

Berdasarkan laporan, on october 9, 2026, japan declared its first-ever cybersecurity state of emergency. A day earlier, ransomware had spread through IDC Frontier, a SoftBank-owned cloud provider, reaching almost 500 client companies and local governments within hours. Across the water, an open-source AI agent was working through seven South Korean banks and lenders, and President Lee Jae Myung told his cabinet there were signs AI had been used.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since then, nearly every conversation i have opens with the same question: “can’t ai just stop this?” in more than two decades in this field, i’ve rarely seen a technology arrive with so much promise. ​.

For years, Japan and South Korea benefited from two defenses that never appeared on an architecture diagram.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first was language. Badly translated phishing was easy to spot, and attackers who couldn’t follow Japanese or Korean business conventions looked elsewhere. That advantage is gone, as open-weight models now produce fluent Japanese and Korean.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the second was skill. In Japan, police arrested three students between the ages of 14 and 16 in 2025 who were accused of using ChatGPT to hijack more than 1,000 mobile lines. Police also arrested a 17-year-old accused of using a ChatGPT-built program to pull 7. 25 million membership records from an internet cafe chain.

Diungkapkan bahwa ai hasn’t produced a generation of elite hackers. Rather, it’s created millions of good-enough attackers and given each the reach of a team. ​.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ​the korean bank campaign used credential stuffing, one of the oldest techniques in the book, run by artex, an autonomous penetration-testing agent published openly on github. It moved through hundreds of IP addresses and altered its timing as it went.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the japanese wave showed the same pattern. One actor moved through hundreds of addresses in under an hour, shaping each request around the previous response. It found nothing exotic: broken authorization, exposed admin APIs, keys left in mobile apps and flaws that already had patches.

Diungkapkan bahwa the ai was the accelerant. The fuel was ours.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if your strategy is to out-model the adversary, then you need smarter models. Your model has guardrails, procurement cycles and a vendor who can switch it off. The attacker’s has none of those. The best open-weight models already match closed frontier models at finding vulnerabilities at a fraction of the cost.

Smarter models matter, but a smarter model pointed at the wrong problem just reaches the wrong answer faster.

Berdasarkan laporan, no single model can protect every industry because each faces distinct attacks. Brokerages are targeted for account takeovers, railways for payment-data theft and operational disruption, and city governments for compromises of the cloud providers they rely on but don’t control. Attackers, entry points and what “normal” looks like all differ.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a generic model trained on broad telemetry erases those distinctions, and that’s where attackers hide. The threat model comes first; the detection model follows.

Sebagaimana diketahui, vendors love to talk about their models. In both countries, the agents kept activity from each address low enough that internal detection saw little worth flagging. Most organizations feed AI internal logs, which describe what has already happened. Few talk about what the model can see. If your data begins at the perimeter, so does your AI.

What matters is outside-in data—what’s being discussed, sold, scanned and staged about you before the first packet arrives.

Diungkapkan bahwa every category is growing, but ai-enabled threats include ai-assisted phishing and reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, malware, semi-autonomous operations and autonomous ransomware. North Korea’s Kimsuky group used ChatGPT to help forge a South Korean military ID. In November 2025, Anthropic disclosed a campaign in which AI carried out an estimated 80% to 90% of the tactical work.

The discipline is to pick the vectors that matter to your sector, geography and exposure, and then build depth there.

Sebagaimana diketahui, attackers think in paths; defenders too often think in lists. A list tells you that you have 4,000 vulnerabilities. A path tells you that a mobile app leaks a key, the key opens an admin API and the API can export your customer table. The only fair response is to map the routes first and break the earliest, cheapest link.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ai is remarkably good at this if it has a reliable asset inventory, a third-party map, the business logic and a view of who’s interested in you. Without that context, it’s guessing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, is ai enough on its own to defend against cyberattacks? no, and i say that as someone who has built a company around ai-driven intelligence. AI is now necessary because machine-speed adversaries can’t be met at human speed, but it’s a multiplier, and multiplying zero still gives you zero.

Diungkapkan bahwa the incidents in japan and south korea showed that the attacker’s advantage was never the model. A smarter model won’t change that. What remained was everything we had failed to fix, and machines found it in hours. Knowing your industry’s real threats, the paths to what matters most and what the outside world already knows about you will.

The question for every CXO and board is: What does an attacker’s AI already know about you that yours doesn’t? That’s what an external threat assessment is for: identifying the exposed assets, leaked credentials, contractor weaknesses and industry-specific paths that machines can now find and exploit in hours and turning them into the outside-in data, vectors and attack paths your AI should be watching.

Diungkapkan bahwa the attackers in japan and south korea won because their ai knew us better than ours did. Until that changes, a smarter model just gives us a faster way to be surprised.

Diungkapkan bahwa forbes technology council is an invitation-only community for world-class cios, ctos and technology executives. Do I qualify?.
